name: live-set-churn
axis: GC heap sizing under a held-alive table — a live set of structs kept for the whole run plus one small struct allocated per unit of work in a hot loop (plumb's x86 decoder's shape: an Insn plus a small operand list per instruction, over a live symbol table)
n: LIVE=50,000 (a live table of ~50,000 three-field structs), CHURN=75,000,000 short-lived allocations — the docs/internals/perf-decoder-gap-2026-09.md §3 reproduction (LIVE unchanged, CHURN scaled 3.75x for ~1s)
nPython: LIVE=5,000, CHURN=3,000,000 — 10x fewer live, 25x fewer churn
notes: This is a HOST-config finding, not a VL code defect: wasmtime's copying collector only grows its GC heap once the live set nearly fills a semispace, so a heap that starts at 0 collects (re-copying the whole live table each time) every few MiB of churn instead of once the live set is actually full. #3022 fixed it for `vl run` by starting the user-program engine's heap at 64 MiB, raised to 256 MiB by docs/internals/perf/gc-heap-policy-2026-09.md; `tests/vl_gc_heap_shape_test.ts` is the fast regression guard (graded by collection COUNT, not wall clock). None of this suite's other kernels could have caught it — their live sets are tiny. Only `t.a`/`t.b` are read off each churn allocation, `t.c` is dead (matching the decoder's asymmetric field usage: not every field of an Insn/Opnd is read every time). The accumulator is pure addition, so Rust/JS/Python fold to i32 once at the end (matching arith/i32-accum's technique) rather than emulating VL's per-op wasm i32 wrap. Scale-verified: doubling CHURN gives VL 2.1x CPU.
